cpfair.title: cpfair/quran-tajweed rule list (counts per madd type)

hamzat_wasl.what: A connecting hamza at the start of some words.
hamzat_wasl.how: If you begin reading at this word, pronounce it. If you join the word to the one before, it drops out and the sound runs straight on.
hamzat_wasl.label: Hamzat al-waṣl

lam_shamsiyyah.what: The lām of “al-” before a “sun letter”.
lam_shamsiyyah.how: The lām is written but not said: it blends into the next letter, which you pronounce doubled.
lam_shamsiyyah.label: Lām shamsiyyah

silent.what: A letter kept in the written muṣḥaf that is not part of the recitation.
silent.how: Read past it. It is not pronounced, whether you carry on or stop.
silent.label: Silent letter

madd_2.what: The natural lengthening of a long vowel (alif, wāw or yāʾ of madd) with no hamza or sukūn after it.
madd_2.how: Hold the long vowel for 2 counts.
madd_2.label: Natural madd (2)

madd_246.what: A long vowel, or a wāw or yāʾ sākinah after a fatḥah (līn), followed by a letter that becomes silent only because you stop on the word, as at the end of an āyah.
madd_246.how: When stopping, you may hold it for 2, 4 or 6 counts.
madd_246.label: Madd ʿāriḍ / līn (2, 4, 6)

madd_munfasil.what: A long vowel ends one word and the next word begins with a hamza.
madd_munfasil.how: In Ḥafṣ it may be held 4 or 5 counts (shortening to 2 is also transmitted). The colouring here follows the 4–5 reading.
madd_munfasil.label: Madd munfaṣil (4–5)

madd_muttasil.what: A long vowel followed by a hamza in the same word.
madd_muttasil.how: In Ḥafṣ, hold it for 4 or 5 counts.
madd_muttasil.label: Madd muttaṣil (4–5)

madd_6.what: The necessary madd: a long vowel followed by a letter with a shaddah or a lasting sukūn.
madd_6.how: Always hold it for 6 counts, whether you carry on or stop.
madd_6.label: Madd lāzim (6)

ghunnah.what: A nasal hum that resonates in the nose. This colour marks a doubled nūn or mīm (with shaddah).
ghunnah.how: Hold the doubled nūn or mīm with that nasal sound for 2 counts.
ghunnah.label: Ghunnah

ikhfa.what: A nūn sākinah or tanwīn before one of the fifteen letters not covered by the other nūn rules.
ikhfa.how: Do not fully pronounce the n. Hide it in a nasal hum (ghunnah, about 2 counts), then move to the next letter.
ikhfa.label: Ikhfāʾ

ikhfa_shafawi.what: A mīm sākinah followed by bāʾ.
ikhfa_shafawi.how: Do not close the lips fully on the mīm; carry it with ghunnah into the bāʾ.
ikhfa_shafawi.label: Ikhfāʾ shafawī

idghaam_ghunnah.what: A nūn sākinah or tanwīn followed by ي ن م or و.
idghaam_ghunnah.how: Merge the n completely into that next letter, keeping the nasal hum (ghunnah) as you do.
idghaam_ghunnah.label: Idghām with ghunnah

idghaam_no_ghunnah.what: A nūn sākinah or tanwīn followed by ل or ر.
idghaam_no_ghunnah.how: Merge the n completely into the ل or ر, with no nasal hum.
idghaam_no_ghunnah.label: Idghām without ghunnah

idghaam_shafawi.what: A mīm sākinah followed by another mīm.
idghaam_shafawi.how: The two become one doubled mīm, held with ghunnah.
idghaam_shafawi.label: Idghām shafawī

idghaam_mutajanisayn.what: Two letters made at the same point in the mouth but with different qualities (such as ت, ط and د).
idghaam_mutajanisayn.how: When the first is sākin, merge it into the second.
idghaam_mutajanisayn.label: Idghām mutajānisayn

idghaam_mutaqaribayn.what: Two letters made at nearby points in the mouth.
idghaam_mutaqaribayn.how: Merge the first into the second.
idghaam_mutaqaribayn.label: Idghām mutaqāribayn

iqlab.what: A nūn sākinah or tanwīn followed by bāʾ.
iqlab.how: Turn the n into a mīm sound, lips not fully closed, held with ghunnah, then say the bāʾ.
iqlab.label: Iqlāb

qalqalah.what: One of the five letters ق ط ب ج د when it is sākin.
qalqalah.how: Release it with a slight bounce or echo so it is heard clearly, not swallowed.
qalqalah.label: Qalqalah
